root_causes: Excessive use of Wait[None] by Agent 0 while still holding objects (toy_fire_truck_0, later toy_food_2), leading to idle time and unnecessary steps.
Inefficient coordination between the two agents: one agent often waits instead of parallelizing remaining subtasks, despite multiple pending propositions.
Replanning loops (repeated replan_post_window and td_error_peak states) indicate instability or over-sensitivity in the planner, causing repeated similar actions and extra navigation.
Cost-insensitive action selection: the policy optimizes for task completion but does not effectively penalize long waits and redundant replans, resulting in a high negative total reward.
improvement_suggestions: Introduce an explicit penalty and heuristic to strongly discourage Wait[None] when the agent is holding a task-relevant object or when unfulfilled propositions remain.
Improve multi-agent coordination so that when one agent is executing a rearrange, the other actively seeks and executes another pending subgoal instead of waiting.
Stabilize the replanning logic by adding hysteresis or thresholds (e.g., minimum state change before replan) to avoid tight replan loops around the same high-level action.
Incorporate reward shaping that directly reflects efficiency (distance, time, number of replans) so the policy learns to minimize idle steps and redundant navigation.
Add a simple high-level scheduler that tracks which propositions are complete and assigns remaining subtasks explicitly to agents to ensure better parallelism and fewer waits.
overall_assessment: All task goals were ultimately satisfied, but the execution contained substantial inefficiencies, with repeated waiting and replanning leading to a large negative reward despite success. The trajectory is functionally correct but operationally suboptimal.
task_instruction: Move the toy fire truck to the chest of drawers. Put the toy food items in a new chest of drawers. Place the stuffed toy on the bed.
